# Slide Blueprint: Gamify Your In-Class Live Quiz

**Generated by:** Skill 04 — Slides Generation
**Workshop slug:** gamify_live_quiz
**Total slides:** 6
**Deck tone:** Bold, high-energy, game-native — confident and direct, never childish
**Color palette:** Deep violet (#1E0A3C) + electric lime (#C6F135) + white (#FFFFFF) + amber (#F5A623) as timer/accent
**Font suggestion:** Headings: Space Grotesk Bold / Body: Space Grotesk Regular (or fallback: Inter Bold / Inter Regular)

---

## Visual System

The deck borrows the visual grammar of modern game UI — bold type, high contrast, dark backgrounds with electric accent pops — while staying fully professional. Think "the settings screen of a well-designed mobile game" rather than "a kindergarten quiz night." Every slide uses the deep violet base; electric lime is used exclusively for the one element that needs to dominate attention (the question, the task prompt, the key concept). Amber is reserved for the timer badge and the assessing close. No gradients, no stock photos, no clipart. Iconography is minimal and geometric — a single icon per slide maximum, used only when it earns its space.

---

## Slides

---

### Slide 01 — Arrival / Title Card
**Phase:** A — Arrival
**Layout:** Title card
**Content:**
- Title: **Gamify Your In-Class Live Quiz**
- Subtitle: *Design one quiz question that makes students actually think.*
- Presenter: [Name] · [Date / Course / Event]

**Speaker cue:** Read your name, the title, and the subtitle (ILO in plain language) aloud. Move on immediately — no backstory, no agenda preview.

**Design Prompt:**
> Full-bleed deep violet background (#1E0A3C). Title in large Space Grotesk Bold, white, centered at 60–70% of slide width. A single geometric game-UI motif in the top-right corner: a minimalist leaderboard icon or trophy outline rendered in electric lime (#C6F135) at low opacity — enough to signal the game theme without competing with the title. Subtitle in smaller weight below the title in off-white (#E8E8E8). Presenter credit line small at bottom center. No gradients. No decorative borders. The overall feeling is: you've just opened a slick app and the session is about to start.

---

### Slide 02 — Reactivating Question
**Phase:** R — Reactivating
**Layout:** Quote card
**Content:**
- Large text: **"Last time you asked a question mid-class and only 2–3 hands went up — raise yours now."**
- Small label below: *Think about it.*

**Speaker cue:** Read the question aloud, then wait. Collect show of hands before advancing. Don't advance until you've acknowledged the response.

**Design Prompt:**
> Deep violet background, slightly lighter than Slide 01 (add 8% white tint) to signal a new phase — still in the same visual world, but the room has shifted. The question text in electric lime (#C6F135), Space Grotesk Bold, very large — occupying 60–65% of slide height. The small italic label "Think about it." in white below at half the size. No images, no icons. The lime question text should feel like a notification on a dark screen — urgent, direct, impossible to ignore.

---

### Slide 03 — Informing: The Core Concept
**Phase:** I — Informing
**Layout:** Two-column
**Content:**
- Left column headline: **"Mechanic + Outcome = Learning"**
- Left column body (small): Two rows:
  - ⚡ Game mechanic alone → entertainment
  - 🎯 Learning outcome alone → homework
- Right column: Key visual — a 2×2 diagram (quadrant) with axes "High mechanic / Low mechanic" (x) and "Low outcome / High outcome" (y); top-right quadrant highlighted in electric lime and labelled **"Live quiz that works"**

**Speaker cue:** Use this slide as a visual anchor while you talk. Point to the highlighted quadrant when you land the core line. Don't read the bullets — they're scaffolding for the visual, not a reading list.

**Design Prompt:**
> Deep violet background. Left column: headline in electric lime, large and bold. Two short supporting lines in white, small weight, with the ⚡ and 🎯 icons in lime. Right column: a clean 2×2 quadrant diagram with thin white grid lines and axis labels in off-white. The top-right quadrant filled in electric lime at 20% opacity with a bold lime border; the label "Live quiz that works" in white bold inside it. All other quadrants remain dark and unlabelled — the contrast does the work. Overall: it should feel like a framework slide from a confident, design-literate speaker, not a textbook diagram.

---

### Slide 03b — Informing: The Rewrite Move
**Phase:** I — Informing (continued)
**Layout:** Full-image (comparison card)
**Content:**
- Top section label: **❌ Recognition question**
  - *"What is the definition of confirmation bias?"*
- Bottom section label: **✅ Retrieval question**
  - *"A researcher only reads studies supporting their hypothesis. What cognitive bias is at play?"*

**Speaker cue:** Advance to this slide when you introduce the example. Read both questions aloud. Pause after the second — give participants a moment to register the difference. This is the "aha" moment; don't rush it.

**Design Prompt:**
> Split horizontally: top half of slide has a deep red-violet (#2D0A1E) tinted background with a faint ❌ icon in the top-right corner at 10% opacity. Bottom half has deep violet (#1E0A3C) with a faint ✅ in electric lime at 10% opacity. The dividing line is a thin amber rule (#F5A623). Each section has a small section label in amber (top: "❌ Recognition" / bottom: "✅ Retrieval") followed by the question text in white, larger, bold. The contrast between the two halves should feel like before/after — red-tinted darkness vs. clear, lime-accented energy. No additional decoration.

---

### Slide 04 — Verarbeitung Task
**Phase:** V — Verarbeitung
**Layout:** Instruction card
**Content:**
- Title: **"Your turn."**
- Numbered steps:
  1. Think of one concept your students often get wrong.
  2. Write one quiz question that requires retrieval — not recognition.
- Timer badge: **⏱ 2 minutes**

**Speaker cue:** Read the task aloud while this slide is showing. Start the timer visibly (phone or projected clock). Leave this slide up the entire time participants are working. Do not advance.

**Design Prompt:**
> Background shifts to a slightly lighter violet-grey (#2A1550) to signal: the room is now active. Title "Your turn." in electric lime, very large, top-left, bold — like a game prompt dropping onto the screen. The two numbered steps in white, generous line spacing, clear hierarchy (numbers in lime, text in white). An amber timer badge in the bottom-right corner: pill-shaped, amber fill (#F5A623), "⏱ 2 min" in bold dark text (#1E0A3C). The badge should feel like a UI countdown element — game-native, not a clipart clock. No other decoration. The slide should feel like an invitation to play.

---

### Slide 05 — Assessing Question
**Phase:** A — Assessing
**Layout:** Takeaway card
**Content:**
- Large text: **"What's the difference between a question that checks understanding and one that just checks attention?"**

**Speaker cue:** Ask the question aloud. Collect 2–3 responses. Synthesize in one sentence. Close the session.

**Design Prompt:**
> Background warms slightly — deep violet with a very subtle amber undertone (#1E1000 or a warm dark base) to signal the session is closing. The question text in white, Space Grotesk Bold, large — occupying 70% of the slide. A thin amber rule (#F5A623) above the question, spanning 40% of the slide width, centred — like a closing ceremony marker. No other elements. The feeling is: the game is over, the score is in, now we reflect. Quieter than Slide 02 but still sharp.

---

### Slide 06 — Close / Where to go next
**Phase:** Close
**Layout:** Title card
**Content:**
- One bold line: **"Start with one question. Try it next class."**
- Optional sub-line: *Tool suggestions: Kahoot! · Mentimeter · Poll Everywhere · Slido*

**Speaker cue:** Leave this slide up as participants leave or as you transition to Q&A. It's a conversation-starter for anyone who wants to keep going.

**Design Prompt:**
> Return to the Slide 01 deep violet. The main line in electric lime, bold, centred — the payoff of the session. The tool suggestions in small off-white text below, a simple inline list. The same faint leaderboard/trophy icon from Slide 01 reappears in the bottom-right in lime at low opacity — visual bookend. The overall feeling: game complete, level unlocked. Clean, confident, done.

## Design System Summary

**Fonts:** Space Grotesk Bold (headings) · Space Grotesk Regular (body) — fallback: Inter Bold / Inter Regular
**Colors:**
- Primary background: Deep Violet `#1E0A3C`
- Dominant accent / question text: Electric Lime `#C6F135`
- Supporting text / body: White `#FFFFFF` / Off-white `#E8E8E8`
- Timer / close accent: Amber `#F5A623`
- Split-slide contrast tint: Dark Red-Violet `#2D0A1E`

**Image style:** Minimal geometric — flat vector icons, clean quadrant diagrams, UI-native badge shapes. No photography, no gradients, no decorative patterns.
**Transitions:** Simple cut between all slides — no animations, no kinetic effects. The visual punch comes from color, not movement.
**Slide ratio:** 16:9
